questions.stem: A 35-year-old man presents for a routine physical examination to your OPD. He states that he has been healthy except for a bout of pneumonia a year ago and an abnormal taste in his mouth for several months. His medications include vitamin E, Flonase, and occasional ibuprofen for muscle aches. Labs reveal an HIV test that is positive. He undergoes counseling regarding his diagnosis. More tests are ordered. The patient's CD4 count is 125, and his viral load is 36,000; he is Toxoplasma gondii IgG positive, and Coccidioides IgG positive. His hepatitis panel shows hepatitis B surface antibody positive and hepatitis C antibody negative. His G6PD screen is negative. He has a tuberculin skin test (TST) reaction measuring 6 mm. You start antiretroviral therapy, and the patient wishes to start all prophylactic treatments for opportunistic infections he is eligible for today. Which medications should be started?

options.label: A
options.text: TMP-SMX for Pneumocystis jiroveci prophylaxis and Fluconazole for coccidioidomycosis prophylaxis

options.label: B
options.text: TMP-SMX for Pneumocystis jiroveci prophylaxis and azithromycin for Mycobacterium avium complex

options.label: C
options.text: TMP-SMX for Pneumocystis jiroveci, azithromycin for Mycobacterium avium complex, and dapsone for T. gondii

options.label: D
options.text: TMP-SMX for Pneumocystis jiroveci and isoniazid for latent tuberculosis
